name: Playwright, Selenium, Cypress
note: Questions authored by Claude as practice material. Not sourced from your own notes or any official exam. Verify anything you doubt against the docs.

options: Waits for elements to be actionable before acting
questions.why: Actions wait for visible, enabled, stable elements.

questions.q: Which Playwright locator style is generally recommended first?
questions.why: Role and text locators survive markup changes better.

questions.q: In Selenium, which is better than time.sleep() for waiting?
questions.why: Explicit waits poll for a condition.

questions.q: Which command records actions into Playwright test code?
questions.why: codegen opens a recorder that outputs test code.

questions.q: How does Playwright keep tests isolated from each other?
options: A new browser context per test
questions.why: Each test gets a fresh context, with its own storage.

options: A test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without any code change
questions.why: Flakiness erodes trust in the suite.

questions.q: Why are web-first assertions like expect(locator).toBeVisible() preferred in Playwright?
options: They retry until the condition is met or time runs out

questions.q: What is the Page Object Model for?
options: Keeping locators and page actions in one place so tests are easier to maintain
questions.why: A UI change then needs fixing in one class.

questions.q: In Cypress, what happens when cy.get() cannot find an element immediately?
questions.why: Built-in retry-ability applies to queries and assertions.

questions.q: What does page.route() allow in Playwright?
questions.why: Useful to simulate errors and slow responses.

options: Reusing a logged-in session across tests so each does not log in again
questions.why: Log in once in setup, reuse the saved cookies and storage.

questions.q: What does test.extend() do in Playwright Test?
questions.why: Custom fixtures give tests shared setup.
